description: Selected-account WordPress inventory, provisioning, administrator access, progress and removal.

notes.text: Available from cPanel 137; every WPX operation needs wp-toolkit and operates on the selected account. Ownership and prerequisites are server checks, not local guarantees.

One request only: no implicit lookup, retry, polling, collision cleanup, file access, returned-URL fetch, restore or rollback. Supplied strings retain their bytes and are encoded once; null optional inputs omit, while false, zero and empty strings stay supplied. No new range, enum, pattern, URL, address-resolution or password-strength validation. Offline contracts do not establish live compatibility.

Omit login only for an installation with exactly one administrator; otherwise supply an existing administrator from getAdminAccount(). Password and login are sensitive and sent in the POST body. Upstream accepts any nonempty password without its own strength rule.

The source describes passing the password through a caller-private file without process-list, process-environment or WordPress Toolkit log exposure. This is documented behavior, not observed live evidence.

Creates a cPanel API token and a Nova magic link; it neither installs WordPress nor queues an installation. A later importWebsite callback starts the import. Requires nova-wordpress, mysql, redirects, apitokens and disk headroom; the source says it does not enforce the WordPress website-count limit. The source attributes token revocation on Nova failure; this is not live evidence. Collision queues nothing.

promptToken is opaque caller-supplied base64: upstream supports standard/URL-safe variants with optional padding, at most 8192 sent characters and 5000 decoded bytes. The client never decodes or re-encodes. Omission or a blank prompt may consume a session prompt; a supplied nonblank prompt leaves that fallback intact.

Upstream returnUrl must be HTTPS on the same cPanel host, with no userinfo and at most 2048 characters. Invalid values are ignored for a default, not rejected locally. The prompt, return URL and returned magic link are private; never log or fetch the magic link.

Requires redirects, mysql, disk headroom and plan website-count allowance. The server normalizes the owned domain, which must have its own document root; the client forwards it unchanged. Omitted title defaults to the domain. Invalid title length/control characters can fail in the background after API success.

Collision is a successful result that queues nothing. Running returns task_id and install_id without proving completion or health. The client never deletes an existing installation automatically. Use getTaskProgress(installId) explicitly; the SSE path needs an interactive session, not an API token.

Each call mints a fresh one-use login token, consumed on first login. It never returns a WordPress password; the source describes empty login/password strings, while their formal string shapes are preserved. Empty login_url is meaningful. Never log or fetch the returned login URL.

Upstream panelReturnUrl must be HTTPS on the same cPanel host, without userinfo and at most 2048 characters; rejected values are ignored for a default. The client forwards it unchanged in the POST body.

Despite its getter name and selected source GET, this token-minting operation uses form POST under mutation policy. Live POST acceptance is unestablished; a GET-only server will fail until route-specific evidence corrects transport.

Requires nova-wordpress plus redirects, wp-toolkit and mysql, an HTTPS source resolving only to public addresses, and an owned destination domain with its own document root. These are server prerequisites; the client does not resolve or fetch the source URL. Source URL/user/password are sensitive and source_user/source_password are body-only.

Omitted overwrite uses upstream default 0; explicit false sends 0, while true can replace an existing installation. passwordType remains a supplied string. The background import can fail after API success. Collision queues nothing; running identifiers are not completion or health. Explicit getTaskProgress(installId) works for API tokens; the SSE path needs an interactive session.
